title: Is Energy Guidance All You Need? Training-Free Norm Injection for Driving World Models

output_modality.value: future driving video jointly with a planned ego trajectory (4 past frames, 8 predicted frames)

control_signal.value: differentiable driving-norm energy on the ego trajectory; demonstrated with an MSE attraction toward a counterfactual braking target

control_mechanism.value: training-free sampling-time guidance: energy gradient on the one-step clean trajectory estimate becomes a velocity correction on the ego stream, with clipping and an asymmetric schedule

base_model.value: Open-Sora 2.0 MM-DiT (DC-AE variant, about 11B) frozen with LoRA rank 16; text stream repurposed for ego trajectory; 19 double-stream blocks used, 38 single-stream bypassed

metrics.value: L2 distance of ego plan to brake target; per-frame optical-flow difference between guided and unguided video. FVD planned, not yet reported.

controllability_evidence.value: Over 35 clips the guided trajectory ends a mean 1.3 m from the brake target versus 13.6 m unguided, but video optical flow changes by 2% or less, so the video does not follow.

closed_loop.value: No; no policy rollout. Single open-loop sampling of 8 future frames from 4 past frames.

stated_limitations.value: Video does not follow steered trajectory (cross-stream coupling); one-step estimate is unreliable early and under multimodality; ODE sampling lacks self-correction; only a single energy tested.

notes: Short workshop-style paper. Control acts on the trajectory, not the video. nuScenes appears only in the reference list, so dataset use is unclear.
